newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson warned about HIV test - Times.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson warned about HIV test - Times.

text.p: Federal regulators warned Johnson & Johnson to clean up its quality control proceedures in the months before the company pulled a controversial home H.I.V. test from the market, The New York Times said.
In Thursday's edition, the Times said the company's Direct Access Diagnostics unit said last week that it was withdrawing the test, called Confide, due to weak sales.
But the formal warnings from the Food and Drug Administration may have been the last straw for the product, the newspaper said.
Among the agency's concerns was the fact that the company was using blood that had been frozen and thawed rather than fresh blood to validate test results.
The company was quoted as saying the FDA's concerns were not factors in discontinuing the test.
